title: In vivo analysis of FBXO45-mediated fibrosis and liver tumorigenesis in a chemically induced mouse model of hepatocellular carcinoma
protocol: Weigh each wild type (WT) and FBXO45-OE mice aged at 14 days.
Dilute the DEN stock solution 40 times to obtain a working solution at a concentration of 2.5 mg/mL.
Calculate the dose of DEN based on the body weight of each mouse (25 mg/kg).
Load the 1 mL syringe with solution.
Tap the syringe and press the plunger slowly to expel the air.
Disinfect the abdomen surface of mice with 70% ethanol.
Gently immobilize the mouse neck with index and thumb finger, while the pinky and ring finger are used to prevent them from moving.
Inject DEN solution or saline intraperitoneally at a 45° angle.
Dilute CCl4 on the day of administration in olive oil in a ratio of 1:4 to obtain a final concentration of 20%.
Calculate and administer CCl4 at a volume of 0.5 mL/kg for each mouse.
Administer CCl4 or vehicle (olive oil) twice weekly for 14 weeks starting at 4 weeks of age, two weeks after DEN injection.
Monitor the health condition of mice daily after injection; provide supportive care if necessary.
Weigh all mice before tissue sample collection.
Anesthetize mice with isoflurane and sacrifice by cervical dislocation.
Shave the abdominal fur of mice.
Fix the mouse limbs on the dissecting board with pins.
Disinfect the abdomen surface (70% ethanol).
Lift the skin with forceps and then cut along the mid-line to open the abdomen and chest using surgical scissors.
Separate livers from mice quickly.
Deliver perfusion solution into inferior cava vein using a peristaltic pump for 10 min to flush the inside of the liver.
Rinse the liver with ice-cold 1×PBS.
Observe and count the number of macroscopically visible liver tumors.
Measure the largest diameter with vernier calipers.
Take photos of the liver and tumor.
Record data about body weight, liver weight, number and size of tumors, occurrence of liver metastasis.
Resect different liver lobes for downstream analysis.
Store a piece of fresh tissue in liquid nitrogen for protein and RNA analysis.
Immerse a larger piece of tissue in 10% formalin for 24 hours for histochemistry.
Place the formalin-treated tissue in 70% ethanol for 24 hours before paraffin embedding.
Cut the same liver lobe from the same area in each tissue sample.
Optional: Collect other tissues such as spleen, kidney, and pancreas if required.
Perform paraffin embedding and slide cutting of 5 μm sections for histopathological assay.
Keep remaining samples in liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.
Place a tissue sample into a 1.5 mL RNase-free and DNase-free EP tube.
Add 1 mL RNAiso Plus reagent to release total RNA from the tissue.
Add 200 μL chloroform to the tube and vortex for 10 seconds with an oscillator.
Incubate the suspension for 15 minutes at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Centrifuge the suspension at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully into a new RNase-free and DNase-free EP tube.
Add an equal volume of pre-cooled isopropanol to the RNA layer and reverse up and down several times.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C to precipitate the RNA.
Remove supernatant without aspirating into the red-colored organic solvent layer.
Add 1 mL DEPC water with 70% ethanol to the precipitated RNA.
Synthesize cDNAs by the PrimeScript RT Reagent Kit with gDNA Eraser following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Place the slides on a sectioning rack and bake in an oven at 65°C for 2–3 hours.
Dip the slides into 3 baths of xylene, each for 5 minutes to deparaffinize.
Transfer the slides to 100% anhydrous ethanol twice for 2 minutes each.
Hydrate slides with 95% ethanol for at least 3 minutes.
Hydrate slides with 85% ethanol for at least 3 minutes.
Hydrate slides with 75% ethanol for at least 3 minutes.
Add hematoxylin to the section for about 30 seconds.
Wash off excess hematoxylin with distilled water for 15 minutes.
Drop Eosin on the slides for about 15 seconds after moderately removing moisture.
Transfer the slides sequentially to 70% ethanol solution for 2 minutes.
Transfer the slides sequentially to 80% ethanol solution for 2 minutes.
Transfer the slides sequentially to 95% ethanol solution for 2 minutes.
Put the slides into xylene.
Let the slides stand at room temperature for about 5 minutes.
Drop a small amount of neutral balsam on the tissue.
Cover the tissue with a coverslip.
Slowly press down the coverslip from one side to avoid air bubbles.
Leave dry for at least 2 hours to observe.
Deparaffinize and rehydrate the tissue slides.
Boil the slides in 10 mM sodium citrate with pressure cooker at high pressure for 2.5 minutes.
Naturally cool to room temperature.
Remove the slides and wash them with PBS or distilled water for 5 minutes three times.
Draw a circle of appropriate size around the tissue using the pap pen.
Block in 3% hydrogen peroxide diluted in distilled water for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the blocking solution and wash with PBS for 5 minutes three times.
Incubate with 5% goat serum diluted in PBS for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Add specific antibodies (anti-FBXO45, anti-Ki67) diluted in PBS to the tissue slides at 4°C overnight.
Wash in PBS 3 times for 5 minutes.
Incubate with secondary antibody at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 60 minutes.
Wash in PBS 3 times for 5 minutes.
Incubate with horseradish peroxidase at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 30 minutes.
Wash in PBS 3 times for 5 minutes.
Add 1-2 drops of DAB to the slides.
Observe the degree of color development under a microscope.
Wash in PBS 3 times for 5 minutes.
Counterstain the slides with hematoxylin.
Rinse the slides with tap water 3 times for 5 minutes each time.
Photograph under bright field at x400 magnification.
